proof decomposes the bijection of the configuration set Σ_E into cycles and averages over configurations s ∈ C_j
'The fraction of initial conditions on Σ_E that land on a bad cycle …' — initial conditions are configurations
every finite bijection acting on a definite configuration visits only product states, S(ρ_R)=0 at the aligned bipartition
'H-scramble fails for every bijection in the setting of Theorem A.7's proof, a definite initial configuration with the bipartition aligned to the configuration coordinates'
G11 Page curve: class C; 'Scrambling, decoupling, proper-shell value open' [FULL:5648]

'For all but an exponentially negligible fraction of initial conditions, … equals the Page value …' (Intro, 4a260ca9)

anchor.why: GR:833 proves (by the long-cycle example and its generalization) that every orbit of a definite configuration is product across the aligned bipartition; the B|R bipartition of A.8 is aligned with C_B × C_R, and A.8's proof counts initial configurations. rows.intro_note: Intro L162 reports A.8's conclusion 'for all but an exponentially negligible fraction of initial conditions' and separately says H-scramble fails for definite configurations; it does not say that A.8's counted initial conditions are exactly those configurations, so the reader is not told that the conditional result is vacuous in the setting as stated.
rows.resolution: GR (separate correction): restate A.8 over an ensemble of initial pure states (initial superpositions) or a non-aligned bipartition, recount the excluded fraction over that ensemble, and move the 'fails' sentence to A.8 itself ('H-scramble fails for every bijection in the setting of this theorem when initial conditions are configurations'); mirror the caveat in appendix A G11 and ch19:72. Introduction: replace 'For all but an exponentially negligible fraction of initial conditions' by a statement that A.8 counts initial configurations, for which H-scramble fails, so its conclusion requires initial superpositions or a non-aligned bipartition, which is open.
